evidence.summary: Round 3 (PERF fixes 1-4): new cip_test parity test, 0024 vs 0025 on all 45 protected tables, 720 cells per version (7 read scopes, 9 read/edit pairs: SELECT per product, UPDATE/DELETE counts, INSERT and UPDATE-move WITH CHECK), each checked against an independent Python model: 0 mismatches either version; 266 cross-version differences all expected (90 '' open by design, 176 one orphan row per table under open scopes). Final cip_test run (current_database() = cip_test printed): 466 passed over 54 files incl. listener, scope and N-0065 DB suites, auth/RBAC neighbours, fix-4 consumers and the round-2 broad sample; fix-4 consumers re-run after the CTE extension 43 passed. Rebind-after-commit DB test extended to a one-line user; listener-removed mutation fails it (18 == 2). Fix 4 row equivalence on cip READ ONLY: identical rows under unset/'*'/NB. Self-verification only.

rationale: The access rule is proven cell by cell on every protected table for both migration versions, the sentinel and listener paths are covered, and the perf change is shown row-identical on real data. Limitation: 0025 is not applied to cip; the cip parity spot check is part of the hand-off script (smoke-tested on 0024: 16/16 OK).
